subject: Vendor evaluation — pricing & migration safeguards
messages:
From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-11-02T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Vendor evaluation — pricing & migration safeguards

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. We're finishing a short vendor review and CloudForge just surfaced a new commercial that tightens our renewal. Their offer in brief: a 14-month commitment, seat-anchored tiering, and a migration credit that covers roughly 60% of our first-month usage cost.

Two things we need from Redwood to evaluate parity: 1) a clean comparison showing run-rate per-token economics across our typical sequence-length mix, and 2) what migration protections/credits you would offer if we switched (including any ops warranty or rollback levers).

I've attached our current pricing sheet so you can see their numbers and our historical usage. Also call out any technical risks you see (eg, quantization differences, egress handling, audit evidence). We're on a fast cadence — procurement wants an initial counter by COB Friday.

Thanks,
Daniel
--
Daniel Wu
Director of AI Platforms
Acme Health
Attachment: acme_current_pricing_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-02T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evaluation — pricing & migration safeguards

Daniel — really appreciate the clarity and the sheet. Quick read-through notes: your usage skews short sequences (~70% < 512) with some spiky peaks for long analysis jobs, so we can structure a better-match pricing profile than a pure seat-based anchor.

Two pragmatic commercial options to present now (high level):

1) Committed plan (12 months) + onboarding bucket
- Unit pricing: custom blended per-token rate based on your mix (we'll send modeled run-rate)
- One-time migration credit: up to 25% of first-quarter expected spend applied as dollar credits (applies if you commit to 12 months)
- Ops warranty: 30-day go-live remediation support (live triage + priority capacity).

2) Pilot-to-commit staged credits (recommended for risk-averse buyers)
- 90-day pilot at slightly higher unit rate, then auto-convert to committed rates on conversion
- Staged migration credits: 15% applied at pilot conversion + additional 10% after 90 days of meeting SLA latency targets
- Rollback clause: if perf delta > 20% vs baseline for two consecutive weeks, auto-fallback to a compatibility variant + 60-day remediation credits

Technical asks we need to size the run-rate and migration scope:
- current peak RPS and 95th percentile latency window
- distribution of sequence lengths (percent < 128, <512, >1024)
- which models you run in prod (and any custom weights or adapters)
- whether you use persistent KV caches per user/session and approximate cache size

I've attached a short outline (redwood-staged-credit-outline.pdf) that frames how the credits and operational warranty would be applied. If you want a clean TCO table against CloudForge I can produce that tomorrow; I just need the usage histogram.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to run numbers with your procurement and engineering team — when works?

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-staged-credit-outline.pdf (PDF, 22 pages)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-02T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Vendor evaluation — pricing & migration safeguards

Looping in Finance and Karthik for visibility — Karthik, high-level: staged credits approach looks good but anything >18% effective discount vs list will need VP approval. Also, legal will want the rollback clause to include clear KPIs and a narrowly scoped remediation plan.

Jonas: please make sure the conversion triggers and the SLA measurement windows are explicit in the term sheet. Also confirm whether the migration credits are gross or net of any marketplace fees (Acme sometimes runs through a channel).

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-11-04T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evaluation — pricing & migration safeguards

Jonas — thanks for that. A couple follow-ups from procurement and infra:
- We need the TCO comparison showing 24-month run-rate with egress, storage for KV caches, and expected infra licensing delta included.
- Can Redwood commit to including audit logs (S3-compatible delivery) and a two-year retention option as part of the enterprise package? That was a sticking point for our security team.
- Finally, can you provide a per-token forecast at three volume bands (current, +30%, +100%) so procurement can stress-test the budget model?

Procurement would prefer the staged pilot but wants clearer economic downside protection in the first 60 days. The rollback clause is essential.

If you can get a draft TCO and the forecast to us by end of day Wednesday, we'll route internally and get back.

Best,
Daniel
--
Daniel Wu
Director of AI Platforms
Acme Health
Attachment: acme_tco_request.docx (docx, 12KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-05T11:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evaluation — pricing & migration safeguards

Daniel — putting the pieces together and we can deliver the TCO + three-band per-token forecast by EOD Wednesday as asked. Quick clarifications so we size everything correctly:
1) Confirm whether KV cache storage should be modeled as "ephemeral-infer" (cached in GPU-hosted NVMe for low latency) or "persistent shared" (S3-backed) — that changes egress and storage forecast.
2) Audit logs: we can deliver S3-compatible upload + optional encryption-at-rest and 2-year retention as an enterprise add-on. We'll include both a standard and a strengthened audit package in the TCO.
3) Marketplace fees: are you buying directly or via a channel partner? If via channel, migration credits need to be structured as a bill-credit rather than direct invoice offset.

Next steps: I've created a HubSpot deal for this (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8421) and dropped a preliminary term-sheet to DocuSign: https://docusign.com/xyz/Redwood-Acme-Terms. I'll schedule a 30-min review once we share the TCO — how does Thursday 10:00am PT look for a joint review with your infra lead?

Thanks,
Jonas

Redwood Inference
